codeReview.summary: Well-structured verification script that closely mirrors the existing verify-dispatcher.ts pattern. The script correctly exercises the SubprocessEvaluatorTransport end-to-end with realistic input, supports all required CLI flags (--engine, --verbose, --dry-run, --help), measures wall-clock timing with performance.now(), validates the response against EvaluatorResultSchema, saves artifacts to .flywheel/verify-evaluator/, and gracefully handles missing engine binaries. The 15 unit tests cover input assembly, CLI parsing, schema validation, engine binary availability, and timing measurement. Code style is consistent with the codebase conventions (ANSI color helpers, artifact saving, structured output). The worker correctly identified a pre-existing prompt/schema mismatch in the evaluator transport (buildPrompt() did not instruct the LLM to return all 6 required fields), which was fixed in a prior feature (the committed subprocess-transport.ts now includes all 6 fields with explicit instructions). The script exits with code 1 on schema validation failure, which is correct behavior for a verification tool. All verification steps passed: --help shows usage, --dry-run assembles input, bun test passes (2978 tests), tsc --noEmit clean.

issues.description: After schema validation fails (line 305: process.exit(1)), the script exits before reaching the individual field checks (lines 308-332). This means if schema validation fails, the detailed field-level diagnostics are never printed. The verify-dispatcher script has the same pattern, so this is consistent, but for a diagnostic tool it would be more useful to continue printing field checks even after schema validation fails, to pinpoint which specific field(s) caused the failure.

The engine binary availability test (line 196-223) conditionally runs assertions based on whether claude/opencode are installed on the test machine. On a machine where both are installed (which is the case here), the only assertion that runs is the 'unknown engine' check. The test would be stronger if it used a mock engine registry or tested with a guaranteed-missing binary name rather than relying on environment state. However, the 'nonexistent' engine test at line 221 does provide baseline coverage.

The timing test at line 232-238 creates a large array (10000 elements) via .fill().map() to force measurable elapsed time, but the variable `arr` is never read (dead code). A simpler approach would be a small loop or Bun.sleep. This is cosmetic and doesn't affect correctness.

summary: The verify-evaluator-script feature is a clean, well-implemented verification script that mirrors the verify-dispatcher.ts pattern faithfully. It covers all required functionality: --engine=claude|opencode, --verbose, --dry-run, --help flags; realistic evaluator input assembly; SubprocessEvaluatorTransport invocation; wall-clock timing via performance.now(); EvaluatorResultSchema validation; artifact saving to .flywheel/verify-evaluator/; and graceful missing-binary handling. 15 unit tests provide solid coverage. Three non-blocking issues noted: (1) early exit on schema validation failure hides detailed field diagnostics, (2) engine binary test is environment-dependent, (3) dead variable in timing test. All are minor and consistent with existing patterns. The worker also discovered and documented a pre-existing prompt/schema mismatch in the evaluator transport, which was properly noted as a discovered issue rather than fixed out of scope. Status: PASS.
